subject: Order Form / MSA: Visibility & Logo Use - triage and next steps
messages:

To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Ortega <sam.ortega@clearline.ai>, Legal Team <legal@clearline.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Dec 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft Order Form / MSA questions on publicity and confidentiality

Hi Logan -

Thanks for sending the draft. Our counsel raised a few items on the publicity and logo-use sections that are blocking internal signoff:

1) Public announcement timing - they want a 60-day quiet period after contract execution (we typically do 30).
2) Logo attribution - they only permit the logo in case studies if the release text is pre-approved and they keep editorial control.
3) Reference rights - they prefer an anonymized case study option rather than a named press release.

I've attached the MSAv3 redlines from our counsel. Can Redwood accept a 60-day quiet period or provide an alternate mitigation? We're happy to sign an Order Form pending alignment here.

Appreciate a quick sync - our marketing lead wants to plan the launch timeline.

Best,
Aisha Park
Head of Partnerships | ClearLine AI

Date: Mon, 15 Dec 2025 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft Order Form / MSA questions on publicity and confidentiality

Aisha -

Thanks for the redlines and context. Looping in Marissa (marketing ops) and David (legal ops) so we can triage. Quick thoughts:

- 60-day quiet period: that's longer than our standard 30-day, but we can accept 60 if we narrow the scope of embargoed content to "press releases and public case studies." That would still allow joint blog posts on product integrations earlier with mutual approval.
- Logo use & editorial control: we can add a clause requiring pre-approval of the release text and a 3-business-day review window for ClearLine to request non-material edits.
- Anonymized case study: acceptable as an option, but we should retain the right to request a named quote during renewal discussions - we can add language that permits either party to propose named references with consent.

Next steps: Marissa, can you provide the logo asset guide and a proposed approval workflow? David / Karthik, please advise on specific contract language (I'll attach the redlines I have).

Thanks - I'll hold on scheduling Exec Review until we align on language.

- Logan
Logan Wright
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi all -

Attaching our brand guide excerpt and a lightweight approval checklist. Proposed operational flow (to keep marketing timelines predictable):

1) Redwood submits proposed release text + proposed logo usage 14 days before planned public announcement.
2) ClearLine provides approval/feedback within 3 business days (minor edits) or 5 business days (material edits).
3) If no response after 5 business days, approval is deemed granted.

If you prefer a stricter quiet period, we can accept the 60 days but we'd ask ClearLine to commit to a shorter internal review SLA for marketing materials (3 business days). That keeps product announcements from slipping.

Attached: logo-usage-guide.pdf (official assets) and a one-page checklist we use for customer quotes.

Marissa Cole
Director, Marketing Operations | Redwood Inference

Attachments: logo-usage-guide.pdf (pdf, 240KB)

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Legal Team <legal@clearline.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Dec 2025 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft Order Form / MSA questions on publicity and confidentiality

Team -

I reviewed ClearLine's redlines. For contract wording that balances your ask and ours, propose the following change set (summary):

• Quiet period: replace "30 days" with "60 days for press releases and public case studies; joint blog posts and release blockers remain subject to mutual approval with a 3-business-day review window."

• Logo use: add a provision that Redwood will only use ClearLine's logo per the attached asset guide, and that ClearLine has 3 business days to review and request non-material edits; any material editorial changes will be discussed in good faith (5 business days).

• Reference Rights: add an explicit "anonymized case study" option and a separate paragraph that neither party may use the other's name for promotional purposes without prior written consent; include a renewal-time friendly clause allowing renewed negotiation of reference scope.

I can insert precise redline text into the MSAv3 PDF if you confirm direction. One note: the "deemed granted" approval after 5 business days is acceptable from our side but ClearLine's counsel may push back - flagging for them here.

If ClearLine agrees to the 3-business-day marketing review SLA, Legal is fine with 60 days on the embargo.

- David
David Kim
Head of Legal Operations | Redwood Inference

Logan / Marissa -

Thanks for the quick triage and concrete proposals. I discussed with our legal and marketing leads - we can accept Redwood's approach with the following clarifications:

• ClearLine will agree to a 60-day quiet period for public press releases and case studies provided Redwood commits to the 3-business-day marketing review SLA for proposed materials.
• ClearLine requires at least one named approver from ClearLine marketing on the approval thread; we will provide the approver contact in the next 24 hours.
• Logo usage: ClearLine will provide a "final logos" pack; Redwood must use the assets and comply with the logo-usage-guide.

We are comfortable with the anonymized case study option remaining available. Once David's redline text is inserted into the MSA, we can turn the Order Form and DocuSign process and aim to execute by the end of the month.

I'll send the approver contact and our updated redline PDF by tomorrow.

Best,
Sam Ortega
Chief Strategy Officer | ClearLine AI
